agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: “ANY tree?”, the parking comparison, and the woman's correction. Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: “All of that” points back to the three descriptions on story card 9, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to supply the relevant context itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The earlier cards have said only that their eyes were opened. They have not mentioned nakedness or a need for coverings, so the baker cannot reason out “naked”; the blank tests unseen wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The setup quotes the general curse but gives no context from which the serpent's new movement can be inferred. “Belly” is therefore an unseen word the baker must guess rather than a meaning supported by the earlier cards.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Cards 2, 3, 4 and 9 all require facts not supplied by the earlier cards: Eve's name, the reason for that name, the material of the garments and what God stations at Eden. Only cards 7 and 10 offer a reasonable basis for an informed pick, so most of this stop's choices rely on guessing.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
